summary: Ikko Arai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Komazawa University, supervised for his MA by Shiro Matsumoto, and studied under Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen (2004), Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, and was attested in 2002 as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

Ikuko Tazaki works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. As of 2017, she held posts as a special researcher (特別研究員) at Otani University and as a collaborative researcher (連携研究員) at Kyoto University.

Ikuro Hattori specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, holding a PhD from Pune University. He served as a researcher (attested 2003) and senior researcher (attested 2026) at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen works in religious studies. He studied under René Gothóni around 1985 to 1993, served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984, and held a post as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Imre Bangha is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University, where he also worked (~1997–2000). Around 2003 he became Associate Professor of Hindi at Oxford and Wolfson College, and Honorary Professor at ELTE (~2013).

Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and history. After degrees from ELTE and UC Berkeley, he worked at the British Library (2002–2012) and Cambridge (2012–2023), later holding posts at Hamburg and Zhejiang University (~2023).

Imre Hamar studied at Eötvös Loránd University (MA ~1986–1992) and National Taiwan Normal University, advised by Noritoshi Aramaki (~1996–1997). He was a visiting professor at Otani University (~1996–1997) and became Professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006.

In-gun Kang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, an S.T.L. from Santa Clara University, and a doctorate from Heythrop College supervised by Michael Barnes (attested 2012).

Ines Konczak-Nagel specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She was a postdoctoral fellow at Berlin State Museums, a visiting fellow at Ryukoku University (2012), and joined the Kuča-Projekt at Leipzig University (attested 2026).
Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University in 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Free University of Berlin in 2000. He held a post at Free University of Berlin (attested 2008) and became a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Bucharest, Sacred Heart, Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and University of Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Hamburg and is attested in 2026 as a project researcher (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) there.
Ippei Okamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Toyo University (attested 2014) and was attested in 2026 as a visiting researcher (客員所員) at Minobusan University.

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology and anthropology. She studied at Fergusson College and the University of Mumbai under G. S. Ghurye, later serving as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and at Penn.

Irfan Habib (born 1931) is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1949–1953), and New College (~1954–1958), he served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1953 to 1991.
